setting: A student is meeting with a study abroad advisor to discuss a semester program overseas.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and a study abroad advisor.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Hi, I'm interested in the exchange program in Spain for next fall, but I'm worried about how the credits will transfer back.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: That's a fair concern. For the Spain program specifically, we have an established agreement, so most courses transfer automatically as long as you stay within the approved course list.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: And if I want to take a class that's not on that list?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: You can request a petition, but it has to be approved by your department chair before you leave, not after you come back. Otherwise there's a real risk the credits won't count.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Okay, that's good to know. My major is engineering, will that be a problem, since I've heard the Spain program is mostly humanities-focused?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: It leans that way, yes, but there are two engineering electives on the approved list. Combined with a petitioned course, you could still make solid progress toward your degree.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: That sounds workable. What's the deadline to apply?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Applications close in six weeks, but I'd recommend submitting the petition for your extra course at least two weeks before that, since department approval can take time.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What is the main topic of the conversation?

options.B: How the student's credits will transfer for a study abroad program
options.C: The student's housing options in Spain

questions.explanation: The student's primary concern throughout is whether and how his credits will transfer.

questions.narrator_text: What must the student do if he wants to take a course not on the approved list?

options.A: Wait until he returns to petition for credit
options.C: Take the course as a non-credit elective
options.D: Switch to a different exchange program

questions.explanation: The advisor explains the petition must be approved by the department chair before he leaves.

questions.narrator_text: According to the advisor, what is a challenge for engineering majors in this particular program?

options.A: There are no engineering courses available at all
options.B: The program is mostly focused on humanities courses
options.C: Engineering students are not eligible to apply
options.D: The engineering courses do not count toward graduation

questions.explanation: The advisor notes the program leans toward humanities, though some engineering electives exist.

questions.narrator_text: What can be inferred about the petition process?

options.A: It is usually rejected for engineering students
options.B: It requires more time than the general application
options.C: It is not necessary if the student has good grades
options.D: It must be submitted after returning from Spain

questions.explanation: The advisor recommends submitting the petition two weeks before the application deadline because department approval takes time.
